## Why This Is Asked

Real-world CI gates combine a linter with lightweight policy checks for Dockerfiles; beginner-friendly yet practical.

## Key Concepts

- hadolint integration in CI
- simple policy checks for Dockerfile security
- local verification steps and CI feedback

## Code Example

```bash
# Example policy script
if grep -E -q "^[[:space:]]*USER[[:space:]]+root" Dockerfile; then
  echo "Dockerfile must not run as root"; exit 1
fi
if grep -E -q "FROM\\s+[^:]+:latest" Dockerfile; then
  echo "Base image tag must be pinned"; exit 1
fi
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to translate security policies into policy-as-code, integrate with CI, and reason about multi-tenant risk.

## Key Concepts
- Kyverno cluster policies
- Pod security posture: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem
- Capabilities and privilege minimization
- CI integration with cluster validation

## Code Example
```javascript
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-container-security
spec:
  rules:
  - name: enforce-security-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment","StatefulSet","DaemonSet","Pod"]
    validate:
      message: "Containers must set non-root, ROFS and drop caps"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - name: "*"
                securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  capabilities:
                    drop: ["ALL"]
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test this at scale across namespaces?
- What are common edge cases (InitContainers, sidecars, imagePullPolicy)?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Demonstrates practicalPolicy as code design with Gatekeeper/OPA, multi-cloud awareness, and enforcing both pod and network baselines.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper/OPA policy authoring and constraint templates
- Pod Security Standards implications (non-root, readOnlyRootFilesystem, privileged escalation)
- Per-namespace NetworkPolicy enforcement and centralized egress allowlist
- Local validation and CI integration (dry-run, audits)

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (K8sSecurityBaseline)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8securitybaseline
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sSecurityBaseline
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8securitybaseline
      violation["RunAsNonRoot"] { input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.runAsNonRoot != true }
      violation["ReadOnlyRoot"] { input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem != true }
      violation["NoNETAdmin"] { input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.capabilities.NET_ADMIN == true }
```
```yaml
# Constraint (example)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sSecurityBaseline
metadata:
  name: require-baseline
spec:
  match:
   Kinds:
    - apiGroups: ["apps"]
      kinds: ["Deployment"]
```

## Why This Is Asked

In production Kubernetes environments, ensuring supply-chain security for Helm-based deployments is critical. This question evaluates your ability to integrate multiple security tools—Helm templating, SBOM generation, and image signature verification—into a cohesive CI gate. It tests practical knowledge of enforcing provenance and attestations before code merges.

## Key Concepts

- **Helm templating and values extraction**: Rendering charts to discover all container images referenced in deployments
- **SBOM generation**: Using Syft to create a CycloneDX SBOM that catalogs all dependencies and artifacts
- **Image signing verification**: Using cosign to validate container image signatures against a public key stored in the repository
- **CI gate integration**: Implementing fail-fast behavior in GitHub Actions to block unsigned images and missing attestations

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow for Helm image signing enforcement
name: Helm Image Security Gate

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  helm-security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3

      - name: Install Helm and Syft
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/main/scripts/get-helm-3 | bash
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anchore/syft/main/install.sh | sh

      - name: Render Helm templates
        run: helm template my-app ./chart --values values.yaml --output-dir ./rendered

      - name: Extract image references
        run: |
          grep -rh 'image:' ./rendered | awk '{print $2}' > images.txt

      - name: Generate SBOM with Syft
        run: |
          syft $(cat images.txt) -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json

      - name: Verify image signatures with cosign
        run: |
          COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY=cosign.pub
          for IMAGE in $(cat images.txt); do
            cosign verify --key $COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY $IMAGE || exit 1
          done
```
